title: Audit Custodian: Tiered Ingest, Indexing, and Cost Guardrails for RBAC-aware Streams
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current audit ingestion and storage pipeline is a single-path hot store with limited tenant-aware controls. This leads to unpredictable cost spikes for large customers, slow query performance for historical audits, and insufficient linkage to RBAC v2 and SSO identity contexts for authorization and forensic queries.

Goal: Implement an 'Audit Custodian' that performs tiered ingestion, RBAC-aware indexing, and cost guardrails at the stream-level so we can: (1) enforce tenant/role-specific retention and indexing policies, (2) route low-value events to coldstore automatically, (3) expose admin controls for safe retention overrides, and (4) integrate SAML/SSO identity attributes into indexing for faster audits.

Scope: Ingest path changes (routing and metadata extraction), index partitioning strategy (per-tenant time windows + role shards), storage lifecycle (hot->warm->cold policies), cost bucketing + throttles, admin console controls (read-only guardrails + override workflow), and telemetry/alerts for cost/SLO regressions. Does NOT include full RBAC v2 implementation; will depend on existing RBAC v2 work for policy enforcement hooks.
decisions: Use streaming pre-processor sidecar to extract SAML attributes (idp:role, org_id) and attach tenant/rbac tags before persistence.
Adopt hybrid retention model: per-tenant retained index for last 90d hot, compressed warm for 90-365d, cold immutable blobs after 1y.
Indexing strategy: primary index = tenant_id + event_time, secondary lightweight role index for rapid RBAC scoped queries (no full-text role indexing).
Cost control: implement per-tenant daily token budget + circuit-breaker that demotes non-critical event types to cold path when exceeded.
tradeoffs: Pros of sidecar pre-processing: preserves runtime isolation and allows optimistic routing; cons: additional deployment complexity and marginal ingestion latency (~5-12ms).
Compressed warm store reduces storage costs but increases restore latency for certain forensic queries — acceptable for low-priority events.
Secondary role index duplicates a small portion of metadata to speed RBAC queries at the cost of extra storage and additional write amplification.
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1097 -- admin UI: retention overrides & audit logs
testing_plan: Unit tests for sidecar metadata extraction, e2e test that simulates tenant burst and verifies demotion to coldstore, load test for index write amplification (<10% 95th percentile latency regression), integration test with RBAC v2 policy hooks to validate query gating. Canary rollout with 5 tenants, metrics tracked: ingest-latency, write-amplification, hotstore-cost-per-tenant, query-latency-90/99. SLO targets documented in design link.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag sidecar and retention-controller; 2) Enable for internal tenants only; 3) Canary with 5 staging tenants for 72h; 4) Open to customers with opt-in via console; 5) Default switch over after 6 weeks and cost validation. Provide admin override path with audit trail and mandatory approver workflow (security + compliance).
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar attaches tenant and SAML role metadata for >99.9% of ingested events in canary tenants.
Hotstore cost per-tenants in canary drops by >=18% for identified heavy writers without increasing query-99 latency for hot ranges.
Retention override flow appears in admin audit logs and requires two approvers when bypassing cost guardrails.
No regression in critical ingest path latency beyond agreed SLA (95th percentile +5ms).
